title: Object detection
summary: Predict object categories and bounding boxes from image features.
why: Localizes multiple objects rather than producing one image-level label.
interview: Compare proposal-based, dense single-stage, and set-prediction detectors.
derivation: Faster R-CNN generates proposals then classifies and refines aligned region features. YOLO and SSD predict densely at feature locations. Anchor-free heads regress distances or boxes without a predefined anchor shape set.
DETR predicts a fixed-size set through learned queries and uses bipartite matching to assign ground truth during training. The no-object class handles unmatched queries.

steps.transformation: Heads(features) -> class logits and box coordinates

steps.note: Conventional dense heads use NMS; DETR set training targets duplicate suppression.
steps.transformation: Assign targets during train; select predictions at infer

traps: Coordinate formats xyxy and cxcywh are not interchangeable.
Resize and padding transforms must be inverted before reporting boxes.
Anchor-free does not automatically mean NMS-free.
DETR matching is discrete; gradients flow through the selected prediction losses.
tradeoff: Two-stage refinement adds latency; dense prediction is efficient; set prediction changes training and duplicate handling.
code:
def iou(a, b):
    iw = max(0, min(a[2], b[2]) - max(a[0], b[0]))
    ih = max(0, min(a[3], b[3]) - max(a[1], b[1]))
    area = lambda x: max(0, x[2]-x[0]) * max(0, x[3]-x[1])
    inter = iw*ih
    union = area(a)+area(b)-inter
    return inter/union if union else 0.0

assert iou((0,0,2,2), (1,1,3,3)) == 1/7

variants.title: Faster R-CNN
variants.flow: image -> backbone -> RPN anchors -> proposals -> RoI features -> class + box
variants.detail: Separate proposal generation and region classification.

variants.title: YOLO / SSD
variants.flow: image -> multi-scale features -> dense class + box heads -> postprocess
variants.detail: SSD uses default boxes. YOLOv8 has anchor-free heads; YOLOv10 adds an end-to-end NMS-free design.

CNN -> Transformer encoder -> decoder object queries -> class + box
ground truth + predictions -> Hungarian matching -> loss
variants.detail: Set-based assignment replaces hand-designed proposal matching.

explanations.title: Two-stage, dense, and set-prediction detectors
paragraphs: Faster R-CNN uses a backbone to compute feature maps, an RPN to propose candidate regions, then region features for class and box prediction. An anchor parameterizes a reference box. The RPN predicts objectness and refinements; later heads refine selected proposals again.

SSD and many YOLO designs make dense predictions on feature grids, often at multiple scales. Anchor-free heads avoid predefined anchor shapes but still need an assignment rule and box parameterization. YOLO generations differ; a family name alone does not specify the training or postprocessing contract.

DETR uses image features and learned object queries to predict a fixed set. Its decoder queries cross-attend to image features and output class logits and boxes. Bipartite matching assigns predictions to ground-truth objects during training, which supports set prediction without the usual hand-designed NMS step in the original model.

explanations.title: IoU, box loss, and Hungarian matching
paragraphs: IoU is intersection area divided by union area. Ordinary IoU is zero for disjoint boxes, so its gradient can be uninformative there. L1 coordinates and generalized IoU provide complementary localization signals in DETR-style training.

Hungarian matching minimizes a pairwise cost between predictions and targets. With N query slots and M objects, match M predictions and supervise unmatched slots as no-object. The matching cost chooses the assignment; the differentiable losses train the matched outputs.

For ordinary dense detectors, distinguish the positive assignment policy, classification loss, confidence construction, and inference NMS. Changing any one can affect recall for crowded or small objects. End-to-end detector variants can use different duplication controls.

explanations.title: Trace coordinates all the way back to the original image
paragraphs: Suppose an 800x600 image is letterboxed into 640x640. Store the scale and offsets used by preprocessing. Boxes predicted in the resized coordinate system must undo both padding and scale before evaluation or visualization.

Report AP across IoU thresholds, class-level results, small-object recall, and end-to-end latency including preprocessing and postprocessing. A high confidence threshold can improve precision while reducing recall. NMS can suppress nearby distinct objects in crowds.

For an interview design, state the object size distribution, crowd density, target hardware, batch size, and acceptable miss rate before choosing a detector. A raw model FLOP count does not include memory movement, dynamic proposals, or NMS cost.
